item.title: Grizzlies rookie Cam Boozer sets new franchise record in NBA debut vs. Jazz
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images Grizzlies rookie Cam Boozer sets new franchise record in NBA debut vs. Jazz appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Cam Boozer did not have his shot falling in his NBA debut, but the Memphis Grizzlies rookie still found a way to make history. Boozer finished with seven points, 11 rebounds and five assists as the Grizzlies routed the Utah Jazz 123-103 in their season opener on Wednesday night at FedEx Forum. His shooting was rough, as he went just 2-of-15 from the field, but Memphis outscored Utah by 32 points with him on the floor. According to StatMuse , that +32 mark is the highest plus-minus by any player in a season opener in Grizzlies franchise history. It was a fitting introduction for the No. 3 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft . Boozer arrived from Duke with a reputation as a polished, do-it-all forward, and even on an off shooting night, he found other ways to help. He knocked down 3-of-4 free throws and made his presence felt on the glass, with Memphis’ rebounding helping it build a 13-point halftime lead. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The rookie had only four points at the break, but he kept finding ways to contribute without scoring. Boozer also benefited from a historic night by a teammate. Ty Jerome exploded for 45 points on 17-of-25 shooting, adding seven rebounds and six assists, and took over in the second half with an array of floaters, three-pointers and drives to the basket. Jerami Grant and GG Jackson also provided outside shooting off the bench. The night was also a showcase of top rookies. Utah’s Darryn Peterson, the No. 2 overall pick, made his debut as well and finished with nine points, four rebounds and three assists. Ace Bailey added 12 points, five rebounds, three assists and three blocks for the Jazz. Keyonte George led Utah with 22 points and five assists, while Lauri Markkanen chipped in 18 points and nine rebounds, but the Jazz could not keep pace once Jerome got rolling. For Boozer, the debut offered a glimpse of what Memphis is hoping for . The shots will come, but his rebounding and playmaking were already making an impact. The Grizzlies will look to keep it going when they visit the Golden State Warriors on Friday.

item.description: UEFA Europa League Preview: Juventus vs Rennes – Team News, Lineups & Prediction Allianz Stadium sets the stage for a handsomely-looking UEFA Europa League clash between Juventus and Rennes. After a thumping 5-0 victory over NEC Nijmegen on the opening matchday, Juventus fought back from an early deficit to beat Celta Vigo 2-1 on the road last week. As a result, they head into round three as one of just ten teams with a 100% record in this season’s league-phase campaign. However, Rennes could be a tricky opponent. Like Juventus, Franck Haise’s side suffered defeat in their domestic championship at the weekend. Paris FC eked out a pulsating 4-3 win over Rennes in the last Ligue 1 round, knocking Les Rouge et Noirs off a two-game winning streak in all competitions. A come-from-behind 2-1 home triumph over OFI Crete in the last Europa League round was part of that run, which was a perfect response to a dull 0-0 draw at Sturm Graz on day one. item.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo takes accountability for the Heat's loss in the season opener
item.description: Giannis Antetokounmpo takes accountability for the Heat's loss in the season opener originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . In the 2026 offseason, the Miami Heat made a big addition by trading for Giannis Antetokounmpo. They added a superstar to a good team, which has made them one of the favorites in the Eastern Conference. They had a good preseason, but they started the 2026-27 season with a loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves . As the star player, Giannis has taken accountability for the loss, as he wants to set the tone for the team. Giannis Antetokounmpo shoulders the blame for the Heat losing their first game It was a bad game for the Heat as they lost in a blowout, 131-106. The Timberwolves utterly dominated the game, as Anthony Edwards dominated with 45 points and 10 rebounds. LaMelo Ball supported him with 21 points of his own. For the Heat, Giannis delivered because he had a 35-point performance. However, the rest of the team struggled to contain the Timberwolves' firepower. MORE: Erik Spoelstra wants his dynamic with Giannis Antetokounmpo to progress naturally As the superstar and one of the Heat's leaders, Antetokounmpo has personally taken on the responsibility for the loss. He does not want to see it happen again, which is why he's making sure to speak on the issues from the first loss. "Our effort gotta be way better. It starts with me; my effort gotta be better. Our effort was not as good as it was in the past. I have to be better; it starts with me. I have to set the tone," Antetokounmpo said after the season opener loss . With the team's struggles being apparent, Giannis wants to resolve it as soon as possible. The Heat want to compete for the championship, so if they manage to take care of these issues, they will be golden. item.title: Mikel Arteta admits Bukayo Saka injury 'doesn’t look good at all' after winger limps off during Arsenal's 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich
item.description: FC Bayern München v Arsenal FC - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 - Getty Images Sport Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has expressed serious concern over Bukayo Saka's fitness after the England winger suffered an early injury during Wednesday's Champions League clash in Germany. The attacker limped off inside the opening exchanges before the Premier League champions fought back to earn a battling point against Bayern Munich. English winger suffers early setback Arteta fears Saka faces a spell on the sidelines after his talismanic wide man sustained a suspected thigh injury against the German champions. The Gunners forward pulled up unchallenged while attempting a routine pass in the 10th minute and had to be withdrawn immediately. Wednesday's hard-earned point at the Allianz Arena was consequently overshadowed by the prospect of losing a key player amid a gruelling calendar. Substitute impact precedes German turnaround FBL-EUR-C1-BAYERN MUNICH-ARSENAL Introduced in Saka's place, Eberechi Eze broke the deadlock in the 25th minute from an incisive Martin Odegaard pass after VAR overturned an initial offside flag. However, the visitors led for just 10 minutes before England captain Harry Kane split the backline from midfield to tee up Alphonso Davies and subsequently sent goalkeeper David Raya the wrong way from 12 yards after his shot struck Jurrien Timber's hand inside the box. Sharing the medical staff's initial concerns over the winger's withdrawal when speaking to TNT Sports , Arteta said: "They [the medical team] are a bit concerned. A player who has to come off with a really sharp pain is never good news, but we have to wait and see." Relentless intensity takes physical toll Arsenal eventually salvaged a draw in the 82nd minute when Declan Rice exchanged passes with substitute Viktor Gyokeres and drilled into the bottom corner before Manuel Neuer produced an acrobatic stop to deny Timber a late winner. Remarkably, it marked only the second time in European Cup or Champions League history that the Gunners have scored first, fallen behind and avoided defeat, repeating their 2-2 stalemate against Bayern in April 2024. Logan led Lakewood St. Edward to a state championship as a senior in 1998. I covered him in the state tournament that year. Logan was certainly recruited by some big programs. But at 5-foot-11 with chubby cheeks and a muffin top, Logan was far from a surefire college star. "I had a lot of talent, but I didn’t know how to work," Logan said. "When I first got (to UC), he was calling me the 'little fat kid from Cleveland.' I said, 'I don’t really like that.' He didn’t care. He said, 'Until you get in shape, that’s what I’m going to call you.' " Logan added: "That’s why I wanted to go play for him. It’s rough. It’s tough. He used that to motivate me. He's a genius." Kenyon Martin, another guy who "mastered" Huggins, left UC as the national player of the year after Logan's sophomore season. Logan was fully bought into Huggins' system by then, in great shape and had earned the coach's trust to take over as team leader. And once you've earned Huggins' respect, he'd let players give it back to him sometimes. He and Logan could butt heads and neither took it personal. Huggins would tell beat reporters about Logan: "He gives hope to fat people." "I said, 'What are going to call me now?' " Logan said. "He couldn't call me 'fat' anymore. That's when he started calling me 'Lo.' " Logan ranks second all-time in scoring at UC, sandwiched between Oscar Robertson and Huggins-era star Danny Fortson on the list. Logan got there on sheer will, following Huggins' blueprint of constantly being in the gym, studying film and playing hurt at times. Huggins came to love Logan so much that the coach let the player leave the team for a few days during the 2001 NCAA Tournament. Logan's grandmother was sick and near death when UC was in Southern California preparing to play in the Sweet Sixteen. Not many coaches would do that, a testament to the special relationship Huggins and Logan had built. "He allowed me to take the trip to talk to her, to hug her," Logan told former Enquirer reporter Bill Koch for his 2022 book titled "Huggs." "I’m forever grateful to him for doing that." How bought into Huggins' system was Logan? Logan plans to share a story during Huggins' induction ceremony about when he played with a severe ankle sprain in the championship game of the 2000 Puerto Rico Holiday Classic. Logan had suffered the injury in the second game of the tournament. "It was bad," Logan said. "They carried me off the floor and took me to the emergency room. The doctor diagnosed me with a high ankle sprain, gave me crutches and said I'd be out 3-5 weeks. We're back at the hotel. I'm sobbing. Huggs comes to my room. He looked at me and said, ‘Lo, the doctors don’t know what they’re talking about. We need you to play tomorrow.' " "Tomorrow?" Logan responded to his coach. Huggins said: Team trainer Jayd Grossman "is going to rub your ankle down all night and in the morning you’re going to feel better and we’re going to win this championship." "And it happened just like that," said Logan, who also shared that story in Koch's book. Logan took over that game against 17th-ranked Alabama, scoring 9 of his 13 points during an 11-1 second-half run to lead UC to a 77-74 overtime win. item.title: Bulls on wrong side of franchise history in opening loss vs. Raptors
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Nick Turchiaro-Imagn Images Bulls on wrong side of franchise history in opening loss vs. Raptors appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Chicago Bulls began the season with an aura of hope. That was largely due to the hype surrounding Caleb Wilson . However, Wednesday night showed that the youngsters are experiencing real growing pains. The Bulls lost their season opener on the road to the Toronto Raptors by 43 points, 135-92. In the process, they suffered the biggest season-opener defeat in franchise history, per K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network. The previous mark was by 25 points in 2001 and 2003. The Bulls showed a wide range of vulnerabilities that often come with opening-game jitters, especially for a young, rebuilding team. For starters, Chicago committed 27 total turnovers, including 11 in the first half alone. Caleb Wilson finished with 9 turnovers and Josh Giddey with 5. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In addition, Josh Giddey was overwhelmed by the posterizing Toronto defense. Plus, Chicago didn’t have anyone on the floor who was close to 7 feet tall. After all, Nic Claxton remains out with a hamstring injury sustained in a preseason practice. Also, even though Caleb Wilson got his first dunk , he shot 1-for-8 from the 3-point line and 7-for-21 from the field. Altogether, he finished with 16 points and 4 rebounds. Matas Buzelis led the way with 17 points, including going 13-for-16 from the free-throw line. Also, Jalen Smith, filling in for Claxton in the paint, finished with 15 points and 8 rebounds. Norman Powell scored 15 points in his Bulls debut. Tre Jones finished with 13 points. Josh Giddey only finished with 2 points, going 1-for-10 from the field. He finished with 7 rebounds and 6 assists. item.title: Phoenix Suns embarrassed in season opener, Oso Ighodaro exits with injury
item.description: Oct 21, 2026; Portland, Oregon, USA; Phoenix Suns guard Devin Booker (15) holds back Portland Trail Blazers guard Ja Morant (1) during the first half at Moda Center. Mandatory Credit: Troy Wayrynen-Imagn Images PORTLAND – Some season openers are bad; others are warning signs. The Phoenix Suns’ embarrassing performance against the Portland Trail Blazers fell firmly into the second category. Oct 21, 2026; Portland, Oregon, USA; Portland Trail Blazers guard Damian Lillard (0) drives to the basket during the first half against Phoenix Suns guard Jalen Green (4) at Moda Center. Mandatory Credit: Troy Wayrynen-Imagn Images Phoenix trailed 43-12 after one quarter and 72-39 at halftime, but the scoreboard wasn’t even the most concerning part. The Suns looked a step behind defensively, stagnant offensively and, most troubling, lacked the urgency expected from a team trying to establish a new identity. Oct 21, 2026; Portland, Oregon, USA; Portland Trail Blazers guard Ja Morant (1) drives to the basket during the first half against Phoenix Suns center Khaman Maluach (10) at Moda Center. Mandatory Credit: Troy Wayrynen-Imagn Images Portland dictated nearly everything. The Trail Blazers attacked the paint, crashed the offensive glass and consistently generated second-chance opportunities. Phoenix spent much of the night reacting instead. That is particularly concerning because physicality and offensive rebounding are supposed to become larger parts of the Suns’ identity. Oct 21, 2026; Portland, Oregon, USA; Portland Trail Blazers forward Deni Avdija (8) is fouled during the first half against Phoenix Suns forward Oso Ighodaro (11) at Moda Center. Mandatory Credit: Troy Wayrynen-Imagn Images Their offensive approach wasn’t much better. Phoenix didn’t make its first 3-pointer until 9:37 remained in the second quarter. When the outside shots weren’t falling, the Suns failed to consistently counter by attacking the rim, pushing in transition, or creating easier opportunities. That becomes an important lesson moving forward. Phoenix cannot simply put two of Devin Booker, Dillon Brooks and Jalen Green on the floor and expect perimeter shooting to solve stagnant possessions. Good offenses need alternatives when Plan A disappears. Oso Ighodaro leaving late in the first half with a hip injury, the same hip he injured during the preseason, only added another concern. It was one game. One terrible game. But that distinction only matters if Phoenix treats it like a warning rather than an excuse. The Suns have an entire season to prove this performance was an anomaly. Their response will tell fans far more than opening night did. item.title: Rockets predicted to trade for Mavericks' $118M veteran NBA champion to reunite with Kevin Durant
item.description: Rockets predicted to trade for Mavericks' $118M veteran NBA champion to reunite with Kevin Durant originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Dallas Mavericks are going to be a team to watch early in the season, but not for the reason many might think. It isn't about whether Dallas wins or loses; it's about the direction the franchise decides to take. Kyrie Irving has been involved in trade speculation all summer, and that is likely to continue. However, Irving has been clear that he wants to stay with the Mavericks. “I'm not gonna shy away from saying it's been a little chaotic at times, inside the locker room as well as outside…I'm in love with this place just because of how welcoming it was, not just from the franchise aspect but also the fans, lot of support around the city…We're building something…Having that championship mindset that whatever we face we can deal with," Irving said. If the team reaches a point where it is struggling and Irving wants out, there is a belief that the Mavericks would grant his request. “Masai also has a really good relationship as you mentioned with Kyrie Irving. I think it's the kind of relationship where if Kyrie says, hey, Masai, like, this isn't for me, I think they could work together to get something done. I don't think would be something ugly. I think there would be interest in Kyrie if he's as healthy as he looks,” NBA insider Marc Spears said. If a trade does come into the picture, CBS Sports' Sam Quinn believes Irving could be traded to the Houston Rockets for a reunion with Kevin Durant. “He's 34 and his team's franchise player is 19. Timeline issues don't need to be deal-breakers, but the Mavericks don't control their own first-round pick again until 2031. They have to find longer-term assets where they can, and Irving is their most desirable trade piece. How does a reunion with Kevin Durant in Houston sound,” Quinn wrote. The duo still believe they should have won an NBA Finals during their time with the Brooklyn Nets , but that never happened. Now, they could have another opportunity to make a run in the Western Conference. Irving is in the final year of his $118 million contract with the Mavericks . With Dallas in need of valuable draft capital, trading Irving could make sense if the franchise decides to move in a different direction. The Atlanta Dream have taken control of the WNBA Finals after crushing the Golden State Valkyries, 97-71, in Game 3 at State Farm Arena on Wednesday and gaining the upper hand, 2-1, in the best-of-seven series. item.title: Bubba Wallace sponsored by COVID-19 vaccine at Talladega
item.description: Oct 17, 2026; Avondale, Arizona, USA; 23XI Racing driver Bubba Wallace (23) during qualifying for the Freeway Insurance 500 at Phoenix Raceway. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Bubba Wallace has never been afraid to stir things up in NASCAR, and his paint scheme for this weekend’s race at Talladega Superspeedway is already doing exactly that. The 23XI Racing driver will be running a car sponsored by a COVID-19 vaccine. Wallace’s No. 23 Toyota will carry Kroger Health and Nuvaxovid, a protein-based COVID-19 vaccine, at the Alabama track this weekend. And as you might expect, the scheme got plenty of attention online as soon as it was revealed. Vaccine Car at Talladega NASCAR writer Joseph Srigley shared the paint scheme on X on Wednesday. “Kroger Health and Nuvaxovid (COVID-19 Vaccine, Adjuvanted) will sponsor Bubba Wallace and the No. 23 Toyota Camry XSE this weekend at Talladega,” Srigley wrote. #NASCAR… Kroger Health and Nuvaxovid (COVID-19 Vaccine, Adjuvanted) will sponsor Bubba Wallace and the No. 23 Toyota Camry XSE this weekend at Talladega. : NASCAR Paint Scheme Preview https://t.co/Z1Rsoqw9oN — Joseph Srigley (@joe_srigley) October 21, 2026 Nuvaxovid is a non-mRNA vaccine, according to 1819 News . Wallace’s car runs with a rotating group of primary sponsors throughout the season, including Columbia and Hardee’s, and NASCAR’s official paint scheme preview lists the car as the No. 23 Kroger Health Toyota. Many fans had jokes about the combination of a COVID-19 vaccine sponsor, a fanbase that skews conservative, and a race in the Deep South. Others simply hoped that Wallace would win just to see how people reacted. Wallace’s History at Talladega Talladega has been home to some of the biggest moments of Wallace’s career. In October 2021, he won a rain-shortened race at the track for his first Cup Series victory, becoming the first Black driver to win a Cup race since Wendell Scott in 1963. The track was also the site of one of the most controversial moments of his career. In June 2020, a member of Wallace’s team reported a noose in his garage stall, and drivers and crew members pushed his car to the front of pit road in a show of support before the race. The FBI later determined that Wallace was not the target of a hate crime, as the rope was a garage door pull that had been in place since the previous fall. But NASCAR noted that Wallace’s stall was the only one of 11 with a knotted pull-down rope tied into a noose, and that Wallace and his team “had nothing to do with this.” Wallace, who was born in Mobile, Alabama, has faced plenty of backlash from some NASCAR fans in the years since. item.title: Fabrizio Romano drops major Carrick update, claims situation has changed behind the scenes after “humiliating” defeat
item.description: Fabrizio Romano drops major Carrick update, claims situation has changed behind the scenes after “humiliating” defeat Manchester United sank to a new low in Italy, suffering an embarrassing 4-1 defeat against Como, who are playing in the Champions League for the first time in their history. Michael Carrick’s reaction after the full-time whistle underlined his disappointment at his side’s performance as he went to the away supporters and held up his hands in apology, without his players. With United now winless in seven games across all competitions, Carrick’s tactical ideas are clearly not working, and the gesture in Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia suggests the end of another managerial spell is on the horizon. Fabrizio Romano details behind the scenes crisis at Manchester United Fabrizio Romano addressed the situation on his YouTube channel, explaining why the feeling after the defeat against Como is different compared to other defeats under Michael Carrick . Romano underlined the gravity of the situation after the absolutely “humiliating” loss by saying he is recording the video at 2 am in Italy to reveal the international tension at Manchester United. “Tonight I’m recording this video, and this is at 2 am at night here in Italy. But the real difference between this game and the other games, the real change between this game and the other games, is also in the players,” the Italian journalist stated. “For the very first time we have players at Manchester United not so happy with the current situation. And that’s something that we can consider as a big change compared to one, two, three, four, five weeks ago, when the season had almost started and Man United were already not at the best level possible.” Discontent among players After the defeat at Atletico Madrid, Lisandro Martinez appeared to back Carrick by criticising director of football Jason Wilcox. However, this time, Romano insisted that “there is a feeling inside that not everyone is so happy with the current situation, and I’m also talking about the coach.” It is understood many players are not happy with the technical and tactical approach under Carrick at Carrington. “That’s why I think we have to be very careful with the Manchester United situation, because now we enter into a different territory,” Romano added. For now, United continue to publicly back Carrick, but as Romano highlighted, they did the same before sacking Erik ten Hag and then Ruben Amorim. Given the Red Devils head coach is rapidly losing the support of his dressing room, we could hear an official statement from INEOS sooner rather than later.

item.title: Unai Emery maintains perfect Champions League start as Aston Villa sweep aside Viking 3-1 to extend Villa Park dominance
item.description: Aston Villa head coach Unai Emery guided his side to a third consecutive Champions League victory with a 3-1 triumph over Norwegian visitors Viking on Wednesday. The hosts built a two-goal interval lead en route to securing two home wins alongside an opening away victory at Club Brugge, climbing to second in the standings. Midlands outfit cruise past Norwegians Emery watched his team build upon their stellar 6-0 demolition of Fenerbahce by comfortably dispatching a stubborn Norwegian outfit that held Bayern Munich to a 3-3 draw last week. Ross Barkley and Emiliano Buendia scored before the break, and a Henrik Heggheim own goal sealed the victory, despite Peter Christiansen pulling back a late strike. The result marks a fifth win in six matches across all competitions for the hosts. First-half blitz settles European contest Aston Villa FC v Viking FK - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 Villa dominated the opening exchanges as visiting goalkeeper Arild Ostbo denied Nicolas Jackson before Barkley broke the deadlock in the 23rd minute by glancing in Ibrahim Mbaye's precise corner kick. Buendia then doubled the advantage from the penalty spot 10 minutes later following a VAR review after Zlatko Tripic fouled Alysson inside the danger area. The hosts effectively settled the contest in the 62nd minute when Heggheim inadvertently turned another dangerous Alysson delivery into his own net. Although Christiansen converted Kristoffer Askildsen's cross late on following a successful VAR check for offside, Villa comfortably secured another emphatic statement victory right there on home soil. Historic milestones underline continental pedigree Victory extended the Villans' extraordinary winning run in major European home fixtures to 12 consecutive matches , matching the longest historical streak achieved by any English club this century. The Midlands side also became the first Europa League holders since Manchester United in 2017-18 to triumph in their opening three matches of the tournament. Furthermore, reaching 20 victories in just 30 European Cup and Champions League outings makes them the second-fastest team in history to hit that landmark , trailing only Real Madrid who required 29 matches. This incredible run highlights their status as serious contenders on the continental stage under the former Sevilla and Villarreal tactician. Blockbuster Barcelona clash awaits Villans FBL-EUR-C1-ASTON VILLA-VIKING Having firmly overcome their early sluggish start to the domestic campaign, Emery's resurgent squad sit proudly second in the elite European table after three rounds of fixtures. Their flawless continental campaign will face its ultimate test when they travel to face La Liga leaders Barcelona next month. Until then, the manager remains entirely focused on sustaining their impressive momentum across upcoming Premier League fixtures.

item.title: Victor Wembanyama hopes to rediscover 'fun' after Thunder shut him down Opening Night
item.description: Absolutely shocked at how things played out, Victor Wembanyama never reciprocated Chet Holmgren's Hulk-esque anger. For the first time in a while, the Oklahoma City Thunder got the absolute best of the San Antonio Spurs in a 116-104 win on Opening Night. From the tipoff, Holmgren had it out for Wembanyama. He was glued to his lanky side on every possession. He rejected every chance to get a switch. Instead, last year's DPOY runner-up locked down the unanimous winner. To the tune of 12 points on an ugly 1-of-13 shooting. It was quite the awakening for most of the NBA world. After last year's epic seven-game duel, most figured San Antonio had OKC's number. But this Opening Night win was the start of the Thunder erasing that national narrative and writing their own in favor of themselves. Afterward, Wembanyama broke down what he did wrong against the team he sent home last year. The MVP candidate believes he must return to his dominant playing style. You can't keep relying on pull-up jumpers if you're 7-foot-4. "I feel like it's obvious for me. I need to go back to playing the basketball I like. This is not the sport I like right here," Wembanyama said. "I got no reason to be hesitant, no reason to not be myself. For me, it's as simple as that. I'm good when I have fun." Interesting to hear Wembanyama utter that sentiment. It's the first time in a minute that the Thunder bullied him out of his comfort zone. Usually, the Spurs have successfully spammed pick-and-roll lobs to their best player. But that option was completely sidelined. That's something to watch for in future matchups. Did the Thunder crack the code at putting Holmgren on Wembanyama? Or will the Spurs make the proper adjustments? Don't expect another one-made field goal night from him. item.title: Charles Barkley takes a ‘dangerous’ Kash Patel dig at Shaquille O’Neal
item.description: Credit: Alex Wong/Emilee Chinn - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images Shaquille O’Neal’s ties to the FBI led to a hilarious shot from Charles Barkley as Inside the NBA returned to the delight of NBA fans everywhere. The NBA season is officially back, and while the basketball aspect of that is very exciting, fans are happy about more than just that. Inside the NBA with Ernie Johnson, Kenny Smith, Charles Barkley, and Shaquille O’Neal is back too, and they’re already going viral. Shaq is known for being someone who has varied interests. His post-NBA career involves everything from receiving honorary doctorates, to becoming a DJ and selling out concerts. O’Neal has also had a history of being involved with law enforcement. Barkley brought that up on their first show of the season. Charles Barkley hilariously asked whether he should ‘stand close’ to Shaquille O’Neal because of Kash Patel FBI Director Kash Patel has dealt with several issues during his tenure at the head of the law enforcement agency. One of the lighter moments recently has been when he named the Los Angeles Lakers legend an honorary FBI Special Agent in September. At that time, Shaq even joked that his Inside the NBA co-host Barkley should be arrested. While they were covering the Miami Heat and Minnesota Timberwolves game, Chuck finally responded. “Should we be standing this close to Shaq? He’s been hanging out with Kash Patel. That’s dangerous,” Barkley said, leading to laughter from all his co-hosts. Ernie Johnson added, “Ooh! Ooh! Oh, I didn’t know you were going there. But I should have known you would.” Having the NBA legends back is likely to lead to a lot more moments that will crack fans up. Nothing is off limits when it comes to Barkley, and his tongue-in-cheek comments to Shaq are what make the show what it is. item.description: Moments before the Valkyries and the Dream were set to play Game 3 of the WNBA Finals on Wednesday night, former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom said he was kicked out of State Farm Arena. Freedom’s exit from the stadium came after he declined to stay in a private suite that was provided to him by the Dream as a safety measure. Angel Reese of the Atlanta Dream during Game 3 of the WNBA Finals on Wednesday night. AP Photo/Brynn Anderson According to a statement from State Farm Arena , “Enes Kanter Freedom has contacted federal, state and local authorities, the WNBA, the Atlanta Dream and State Farm Arena officials to express concerns about his personal safety during his planned attendance at Game 3 of the WNBA Finals tonight,” the statement read. “The safety and security of our guests and team members is our highest priority. “Following consultations with the WNBA, Dream ownership, State Farm Arena leadership and security officials, we have directed Mr. Freedom to watch tonight’s game from a private luxury suite. This arrangement is intended to address his security concerns and help provide a safe and positive experience for him and other guests. The suite will have additional security and will be his designated viewing location for the game. State police have also assigned an officer to Mr. Freedom at his request.” ATTENTION! Just talked to director of security of the @NBA and they are now banning us from our purchased seats. Shame on @WNBA I guess they have to escort me out of the building. Stay tuned. pic.twitter.com/f2adrlkWhx — Enes Kanter FREEDOM (@EnesFreedom) October 21, 2026 Before the game started, Freedom posted a video of himself on X with the caption that read, “Just talked to director of the @NBA and they are now banning us from our purchased seats.” Freedom went on to write, “Shame on @WNBA. I guess they have to escort me out of the building. Stay tuned.” Seven Atlanta police officers to stop one man wearing a “What is a Woman?” shirt. @EnesFreedom was physically blocked from reaching his PAID seats at the WNBA Finals, then removed from State Farm Arena. pic.twitter.com/3xKqy8dzGS — OutKick (@Outkick) October 22, 2026 Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected from State Farm Arena before Game 3 of the WNBA Finals on Wednesday night. item.title: NASCAR’s Corey Heim Gets Honest About Bubba Wallace After Costly Phoenix Penalty
item.description: NASCAR driver Corey Heim gave his honest take on Bubba Wallace after a costly pit-road speeding penalty at Phoenix Raceway. Getty Corey Heim said Wednesday that NASCAR teammate Bubba Wallace has moved past the Phoenix speeding penalty that cost him a shot at his first win of 2026, and 23XI Racing is heading to Talladega with fresh optimism. Wallace led 52 laps Sunday, his most in any race this season, yet left Phoenix winless once again, which leaves the team one week to regroup before the unpredictable YellaWood 500. “I think it’s really optimistic, especially after Tyler was able to get back to victory lane,” Heim said Wednesday on SiriusXM NASCAR Radio, as quoted by On3‘s Jamie Oakes. Tyler Reddick of 23XI won Sunday’s Freeway Insurance 500, his sixth victory of 2026 and the end of a 23-race winless stretch, according to NASCAR.com. Heim finished fifth. Read More From Heavy NASCAR Handed Troubling TV Ratings News After Phoenix Cup Series Race Bubba Wallace’s Phoenix Speeding Penalty “Same with Bubba, I mean, he’s had great speed, but one thing or another will happen and they just aren’t able to close these things out,” Heim said. A caution for Kyle Larson’s crash sent the leaders to pit road with 27 laps remaining. Wallace took four tires, left in sixth place and drew a pit road speeding penalty that dropped him out of the top 10. He finished 17th and remains winless since the Brickyard 400 in 2025, according to RACER ‘s Kelly Crandall . “Our team is so good at finding all the gray areas to operate in and find our limits, and I think I exposed it a little bit too much around the corner,” Wallace said. “Corner pitting is really, really tough … just with the lack of visibility that you have.” “I hate it for our team,” Wallace continued. “It’s been really fun driving Toyotas this year, but I just can’t seem to close the deal out. Three more to go.” Heim saw a different mood in the shop this week. “You can just tell he’s so refreshed to have a winning race car at Phoenix with that place kind of being a trouble area for 23XI in the past,” Heim said. Heim will not be in the Cup field Sunday. “At the end of the day, it is Talladega, so we’ll see what happens,” he said. item.title: ‘Don’t do it rook’ – Warriors rookie’s heated exchange with Luka Doncic has fans buzzing after backfiring
item.description: Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images Los Angeles Lakers superstar Luka Doncic sent an emphatic message to Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg for trash-talking him in the first half of their opening-night clash. Lendeborg is making his NBA debut with the Warriors against the Lakers in a nationally televised game. The 24-year-old tried to show he is fearless by taking on the challenge of guarding Luka Doncic, which led to him trying to trash-talk the six-time All-NBA First Team guard. After Lendeborg’s attempt at trash-talking Doncic, the 27-year-old Slovenian responded in the most emphatic way possible. Yaxel Lendeborg’s trash-talk attempt to Luka Doncic ends in disaster After Doncic managed to lull Yaxel into fouling him with less than three minutes left in the second quarter, the rookie started jawing at Doncic, with Luka not afraid to respond. This moment would spark Doncic into scoring nine points over the next two minutes, with the final three points coming with a half-court buzzer-beating three-point heave over Lendeborg. Fans are already mocking the Warriors rookie for poking the tiger and ensuring that Doncic is motivated to destroy them for the rest of the evening. “Don’t do it, rook,” warned one concerned fan . “Does he not know that talking to Luka Doncic is the worst thing you can do?” said a fan . “Yaxel’s welcome to the league moment,” said one fan . “Yaxel gonna learn the hard way,” said another fan . “Lendeborg really woke Luka up in the 2nd quarter. Bad idea, rook. Real bad idea,” mentioned a fan . Doncic ended the first half with 23 points, six rebounds and four assists as the Lakers hold a 66-52 lead over the Warriors. Lendeborg’s first half of NBA basketball has him putting up a respectable five points, two rebounds, two assists and a steal, playing admirable defence on Doncic. Unfortunately, Doncic has far more offensive counters for Lendeborg and the Warriors’ defence than they can game plan for, as Luka got more comfortable on the court as the quarter wore on. item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Now then, which one of you hipsters decided to put Porto 0-1 PSV on? Oh dear. This was another night of Bigger Cup at its Bigliest self, comebacks everywhere, 40 goals in nine games, six of those in a best-v-best clash as Paris Saint-Germain rallied late against Barcelona. Even in defeat, Lamine Yamal found space to decorate the room with a ludicrous toe-poke equaliser, and there was a wholesome tale in Italy as Scott McTominay scored twice for Napoli in their 4-3 win against Bodø/Glimt. These were his first strikes since returning from heart surgery, taking his tally at the club to 29 goals in 86 appearances. No wonder Erik ten Hag was peeved with his bosses at Manchester United for shipping the midfielder off to Naples. One has to admire the courage of Erik ten Hag, speaking out on Man United’s ‘toxic culture’ [yesterday’s Football Daily, full email edition]. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.description: As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry , a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26. Further to Peters and Lee [ Monday’s Football Daily letters] another 70s example that occurred to me was the West Ham players Mervyn Day and Bill Green . They were both in the West Ham United team from 1976-78, and in Carlisle United’s greatest season 1974-75. When Green was still at Carlisle, he played against West Ham’s Day. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning. item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: ‘Miro’, now in charge at Nürnberg, knows the value of consistency and identity in an era of tinkering coaches who did not play professionally You learn the most from the best. The Champions League winners are Paris Saint-Germain, and they could achieve a historic hat-trick this season. Since the tournament’s rebrand in 1992, they would be only the second club to accomplish this feat, after Real Madrid’s run from 2016 to 2018. I see clear parallels between the two. For Madrid, nine players started in all three of their final victories. Similarly, PSG won their two finals with virtually identical lineups. The only change came during their title defence in Budapest , where Gianluigi Donnarumma no longer featured in goal, Luis Enrique having parted ways with the Italian European champion. core players: about 70 to 85% each remaining regular starters: 50 to 60% each squad players: 40 to 45% each fringe squad places: sharing the remaining maximum of 20% Continue reading...

item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. item.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
